- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce the forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and forecast is falling, avoid underestimating the rebound; add 3–5% to the low end to capture mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive price increases), reduce the forecast’s later days by 2–5% to account for lag.  
- If the model consistently overpredicts after a spike (e.g., +10%+ above true outcome), apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–7% from the forecast’s peak and subsequent days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.1–0.3) and price is near historical mean, favor slight downward bias (−1–3%) to reflect mean reversion.  
- Avoid forecasting “too far ahead” — if sentiment is weak or volatile, cap 30-day forecast at 1.5x the 14-day moving average to prevent horizon drift.
